comparison: All25 accepted alpha reports; conditional partial prices not empirical expected-value ranking.

selected.why: Direct overdose prevention has unusually large plausible health stakes at a modest project budget; its present clinical-only price needs a coherent annual and signed-resource audit, not promotion as verified EV.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: Can matched unique opioid-risk clients, incremental naloxone access versus public supply, finite survival utility and full participant/provider resources support the annual model without an extra marginal-donor multiplier, and is the gift route usable?

selected.why: Controlled sealant efficacy, observable delivered dentistry and relatively small local costs make the missing resource bridge and treatment/cost boundary unusually learnable.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: Can unique children/tooth/retention data and direct dental health plus net caregiver resources replace four-molar equivalents and unsupported DALY-to-QALY transport, with clinical/restorative services and a current donor route assessed?

selected.why: Large native application-household throughput and a resource-oriented mechanism warrant early review, provided approvals, alternative navigation and full taxpayer incidence are not mistaken for donor-created income.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: How many unique Denver households obtained additional sustained SNAP through HFC rather than partners/self-application, with actual net food-consumption gains and full public-payer costs; what implemented school-food effects can be separately bounded?

selected.why: Low annual scale, completed local repairs and volunteer leverage make health/function and actual avoided spending potentially informative despite county leakage and unmeasured utilities.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: Which FY2024 repairs were additional, durable and in the Denver boundary, and what health/function and otherwise-paid resource changes remain after other repair providers, household duplication and full volunteer cost?

selected.why: The high whole-cost partial-channel price can hide a much narrower bill program and substantial household resource flow; known bill costs and current scale offer meaningful value of information.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: Can bill-assistance households and actual cash offsets be matched to the $21.874M recognized channel, while including utility/LEAP/taxpayer replacement, temperature-health effects and separately bounded efficiency/furnace services?

selected.why: Matched patients and current fee information make the balance of clinical access against signed family costs testable, and relevant primary-care mechanisms extend beyond the initial generic response prior.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: Which additional completed primary/behavioral care produces finite clinical benefit versus covered alternatives, with patient health independent of household grouping and actual fees, work/time and payer costs jointly netted?

selected.why: A small support budget and biologically evidence-based prevention mechanism justify reviewing completed protection and partner cost attribution rather than accepting a conservative one-clinic subset.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: What vaccine/age mix, unique completed protection and coalition additionality are supported, and do full partner/public delivery costs plus caregiver/adult resource incidence change the one-clinic partial reference?

selected.why: Documented regulatory engagement and independent rule adoption create a concrete implementation question with potentially wide local reach, but neither monitoring nor benchmark adoption is itself a health result.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: Did Regulation30 move beyond benchmarks to additional implemented local abatement, and what resident exposure/duration, coalition counterfactual, participant burden, compliance and job incidence can be defensibly bounded?

selected.why: Local perinatal programs and controlled prevention evidence offer a decision-relevant alternative to generic counseling, with caregiver resources and actual program dose still unresolved.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: Do original MotherWise/La Luz results and current prenatal/postpartum delivery support a locally compatible clinical effect and dose, rather than importing ROSE or marketing preterm reduction; what net caregiver work/childcare effects and costs accompany it?

selected.why: Existing-patient reproductive choices have primary comparative health and multi-year economic evidence; a high full-regional-cost/local-subset price does not resolve the wider opportunity.
selected.decisionChangingQuestion: Can Denver-resident service/cost allocation and genuine alternative access be established, extending beyond abortion to contraception/other care while testing finite maternal health and after-tax/benefit/childcare resources without assigning intrinsic welfare to births or unborn life?

excluded.why: Promising high-risk access and modest budget, but annual N500 is entirely judged and insurance/I Matter alternatives are unresolved; first alternate if completed annual cohort evidence makes it more learnable than the selected reproductive/perinatal reviews.

Current unique outpatient count is useful, but cost-vintage mismatch, usual-care counseling alternatives and generic utility transfer offer less immediate comparative information than selected matched clinical and targeted prevention pathways; not ruled ineffective.

Assess transport safety, commuting costs and public-payer/job effects, but no implemented local project beneficiary cohort and broken donation route currently make the policy causal chain less bounded than Cultivando’s named rulemaking test; public agencies remain the central alternative.

Potentially large net resource/insurance welfare, but discontinued food delivery makes historical costs incompatible with current navigation and mixed individuals/families/applications obscure approvals; HFC offers a fresher matched service/cost starting point.

Real historical assistance is observable, but nominal bill savings are not collectible consumption and providers may lose the same cash; current cohort and policy implementation are unresolved, so HFC/EOC have clearer resource-flow questions first.

Volunteer counseling may be valuable, but connections versus actual completed patients, parent support and broader program costs create several simultaneous unit/boundary uncertainties relative to the selected targeted mechanisms.

Strong matched treatment-client and session data make this a close clinical alternate; utilities, household dose and unmeasured forensic/prevention attribution remain similar to other trauma services, while selected perinatal/clinical pathways have more distinct decision-changing research.

Direct trauma support is important, but uncontrolled pre/post changes and partial therapy counts do not identify incremental utility or advocacy benefits; selecting another overlapping trauma-access review adds less immediate information than the chosen set.

MST has plausible benefits but contrary controlled long-term evidence against active usual care and large full-recipient/partial-MST cost scope; resolving early-childhood/foster/other channels and local fidelity likely exceeds a bounded initial deep pass.

PrEP biology is strong, but 557 navigations do not establish adherent starts and the whole HIV-care/nutrition/harm-reduction portfolio dominates costs; public medication coverage and other providers require a substantially different channel boundary, not rejection on its high price.

MAT, crisis and other care may have large omitted effects; broad 24,681 clients/prescriptions and depression-only full-cost reference lack a bounded causal subgroup. It is an important alternate if local completed MAT/crisis evidence becomes available.

Integrated bilingual care has promising access benefits, but the depression subgroup/dose is judged and full primary/dental/pharmacy effects remain unquantified; Doctors Care offers matched costs/patients and concrete fee incidence for the first clinical review.

Dental clinical benefits are plausible, but national donation allocation and stale state completions prevent a current Denver-specific funding comparison; KIND provides a more concrete local prevention/clinical starting point.

Actual 25 youth jobs, therapy completions and incident responses merit health-plus-net-income assessment, but no incremental wage/hours or unique injury cohort and uncertain violence trials currently limit learnability; exclude for evidence/alternative-VOI limits, not the high partial price.

School therapy, caregiver access and TREE employment may be substantial, but 63 school-served students against whole statewide costs omit most activity and provide no completed clinical or net job outcome; district-funded school and covered-care alternatives are unresolved, not presumed no benefit.
